messages:
alex_customer: Hey team — we've got recurring reports from customers using our Editor Assist extension (VSCode) where long streaming responses abruptly end and show as a 5xx in billing. One user repro: large code-generation prompt, 3-4k tokens, then VSCode shows "connection reset", logs show:

alex_customer: ```
Client: EditorAssist v2.1.3
Request: POST /v1/stream?model=redwood-code-7b
Headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Server log: proxy: write tcp ... broken pipe
Gateway: marked as 502
```

maria_support: Thanks Alex. Can you paste a minimal repro that we can run locally? Any proxy or intermediary in front of the extension? :thinking:

alex_customer: Yep repro steps below — happens ~40% of attempts with long streaming output. Steps:
1) Open EditorAssist
2) Run large snippet generation (~3-4k tokens)
3) Observe stream abort ~20-40s in

alex_customer (continued): Curl repro they used: ```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -d @prompt.txt https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```

devin_sre: Noted. I pulled the gateway logs for the user session id they included — I see a FIN race from client side followed by proxy write failing: `write: broken pipe` and gateway marks as upstream error -> 5xx. Our current heuristics may be too aggressive in labeling these as server 5xx.

devin_sre (continued): Do we have the client's IP? Could their editor be closing prematurely due to keepalive or an extension-level cancel?

alex_customer: Client IP 203.0.113.45, behind corp NAT + a small extension proxy. I also see VSCode extension logs showing a 200-stream started then sudden `ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED`.

junaid_runtime: I suspect our proxy's chunked encoding framing plus extension's small buffer leads to a halfclose race. If client half-closes but TCP FIN arrives before all chunks flushed, some proxies surface as write error upstream. We recently tightened write timeouts on the gateway (PR #4521). Could be related.

maria_support: Can eng-runtime try to reproduce with EditorAssist v2.1.3 and our gateway config (write_timeout=5s)? If it's a timeout sensitivity issue, we can widen window or alter EOF handling heuristics.

junaid_runtime: Reproduced locally with a simulated slow consumer (throttled read) in EditorAssist. I can trigger `write: broken pipe` when consumer pauses and we hit the 5s write timeout. Logs attached: `gateway: upstream write error, class=5xx`.

infra-bot: deploy:gateway/timeout-config rolled back to previous value at 3612349000 by devops for investigation. :wrench:

olivia_billing: Re billing — when gateway marks as 5xx we currently zero-rate those requests but billing UI still shows a 5xx tag which leads customers to dispute. We should avoid labeling client-abort as upstream 5xx in metering.

devin_sre: Proposed fix: change classification so if upstream logged 'broken pipe' and tcp reset seen from client side within 1s, treat as client disconnect and classify as aborted (not 5xx). Need runtime confirmation this won't hide real upstream errors.

alex_customer: That sounds good. Customer impact: a handful of paid customers saw sudden credit usage + 5xx label, created support tickets. Any ETA?

junaid_runtime: I can push a canary to staging today that changes metrics classification and adds an extra tag `cause=client_halfclose` for debugging. If passes, we can roll to prod with a short window.

maria_support: I'll notify customers and escalate to priority so billing doesn't auto-charge. Olivia, can we proactively credit affected accounts if we flip classification?

olivia_billing: Yes — if we confirm misclassification we'll issue credits. Send me a list of affected request IDs.

alex_customer: Thanks all — attaching one of the full logs and request_id 0f4b2a7c for follow-up. Will test the staging canary and report back. :+1:
